Definition: from G2919; a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")):--avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment.
KeyPassages: Romans 11:33; 1 Peter 4:17; 1 Corinthians 11:29; 2 Peter 2:3; Hebrews 6:2; 1 Timothy 3:6
BiblicalUsage: Krima is the judgment or sentence itself, the decision handed down. Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 11:29 that eating unworthily brings damnation on oneself, Peter says judgment must begin at the house of God in 1 Peter 4:17, Paul tells Timothy a novice may fall into "the condemnation of the devil" in 1 Timothy 3:6, and Hebrews 6:2 lists "eternal judgment" among the foundations of the doctrine of Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: For me, judgment is not a threat God waves at the world; it begins with His own house, and that is why I take the Lord's table and the church's order seriously. That is why I come to the table with fear and to the judgment with hope.
RelatedBooks: Romans; 1 Peter; 1 Corinthians; 2 Peter; Hebrews; 1 Timothy
